newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Analysts remain upbeat on Taiwan Semicon.
newsitem.headline: Analysts remain upbeat on Taiwan Semicon.

text.p: Recent price surges have turned microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co into the island's biggest firm in market value, and analysts said they remained upbeat on the company's outlook.

"Taiwan Semiconductor, already the world's best and biggest integrated circuits foundry maker, no doubt will lead Taiwan to become an island of high-technology," said International Investment Trust vice-president David Yu.

Based on Wednesday's closing price, Taiwan Semicon had a market value of T$567.3 billion (US$20 billion), the largest among Taiwan's 391 listed firms, the local Wealth News securities newspaper reported on Thursday.
Second was rival United Microelectronics with T$547.1 billion (US$19.6 billion) and third was Cathay Life Insurance with T$527.4 billion (US$18.9 billion).

"Taiwan's high-tech electronics industry has been renowned for its flexible, low-cost and quality manufacturing capability, and Taiwan Semicon is the best example," said Jardine Fleming Securities fund manager George Hou.

HSBC James Capel research chief Alex Chen said Taiwan Semicon had already entered mass-production of 0.35 micron processing technology and test production of 0.25 micron technology in microchip making -- a world-class level that no other local microchip makers can compete with.
"Taiwan Semicon is the new success model -- the world's first IC foundry maker -- and the records proves it has succeeded," Chen said.
The firm's custom-order foundry business does not design and sell its own IC products, but manufactures products according to customers' specifications.
Analysts put Taiwan Semicon's operating margin at around 35-40 percent, with its per-share-earnings forecast at T$4.2-4.5 for 1997 and T$5.8-7.0 for 1998.
"Such a high profit return has attracted other local conglomerates to enter the IC field," Chen said.
Analysts said the IC foundry business will have a compound annual growth of 30 percent in the next decade.
The expected high growth in the IC industry has prompted Taiwan IC makers to announce huge expansion projects in the past few months.
In April, Taiwan Semicon said it would build six advanced wafer-fabrication plants as part of a T$400 billion investment at a high-tech park in southern Taiwan's Tainan.
Two months later, United Micro announced plans to invest T$500 billion in a 10-year wafer project.
Analysts said many investors now see Taiwan Semicon as a barometer of the fortunes of the technology sector, which has come to dominate the Taiwan industry and the stock market.
Taiwan Semicon's share price setback on Wednesday helped trigger a 1.77 percent fall in the wider index on that day.
But Taiwan Semicon on Thursday rose by the daily seven percent limit to T$143, leading the overall index up 2.68 percent to 9,632.42 points. (US$ = T$27.9)
